content: Document Reference: PORTPROBE-DOC-PRD-01 Document Version: 2.0.0 Classification: Enterprise Infrastructure Software Specification Status: Official Release Last Updated: November 2026 --- 1. Executive Summary & Product Introduction PortProbe is an asynchronous, high-concurrency TCP connectivity verification daemon and client probe written in 100% safe Rust. It provides infrastructure engineers, Site Reliability Engineering SRE teams, network administrators, and DevOps practitioners with a lightweight, secure, and deterministic utility to validate network reachability, test firewall access control lists ACLs , verify load balancer health probing, and diagnose network routing paths across distributed hybrid-cloud infrastructure. Traditionally, verifying that a newly provisioned firewall rule or software-defined network SDN security group works required either: 1. Waiting for the complete multi-tier enterprise workload such as an Oracle/PostgreSQL database, Kafka cluster, or SAP backend to be fully installed and running. 2. Ad-hoc execution of fragile, insecure workarounds like nc -l Netcat , Python's http.server , or Telnet listeners that lack rate limiting, multi-port support, authentication, logging, and security isolation. PortProbe eliminates this operational friction. By executing as a hardened standalone daemon or an automated client probe, PortProbe allows teams to establish authoritative TCP listeners on demand, verify bidirectional network reachability, and safely teardown or integrate into continuous monitoring without introducing security vulnerabilities or resource exhaustion into the environment. --- 2. Problem Statement: Why PortProbe Was Developed In modern enterprise environments—spanning physical data centers, software-defined perimeters SDP , Kubernetes clusters, and multi-cloud virtual private clouds VPCs —network connectivity provisioning is a multi-team operational bottleneck. The Enterprise Challenges Addressed: 1. The "Chicken-and-Egg" Dependency Dilemma : Application deployment pipelines frequently fail at the final stage because an underlying network route, NAT gateway, or firewall port was incorrectly configured. Infrastructure teams cannot verify connectivity until the application is running, but the application cannot start until its backend dependencies are reachable. 2. Security Vulnerabilities of Ad-Hoc Utilities : Engineers frequently resort to running nc -l -p port or python3 -m http.server port . These utilities: - Accept unrestricted incoming payloads, creating potential remote code execution or buffer overflow vectors. - Lack concurrency limits, making the host vulnerable to connection starvation. - Lack rate limiting, allowing network scanners to consume CPU and file descriptors. - Do not support TLS or mutual TLS mTLS , transmitting plain text across sensitive network segments. - Run with elevated permissions without privilege-dropping capabilities. 3. Load Balancer and Health Probe Verification Gaps : When configuring hardware or cloud load balancers F5 BIG-IP, AWS ALB/NLB, HAProxy, Envoy , engineers need a deterministic backend target that responds correctly to TCP three-way handshakes, TLS handshakes, or HTTP /healthz endpoints without generating application-tier errors. 4. Automated CI/CD Infrastructure Testing : Terraform and Ansible provisioning scripts require a fast, deterministic tool with standardized exit codes to validate that newly provisioned infrastructure complies with network access policies before releasing workloads. --- 3. Product Vision and Core Objectives PortProbe was designed from the ground up to embody five core architectural principles: - Safety & Robustness : Written strictly in safe Rust ! deny unsafe code . Zero memory corruption, buffer overflows, or data races. - Minimal Resource Footprint : Asynchronous I/O powered by Tokio, capable of sustaining thousands of concurrent connections while consuming less than 15 MB of resident memory RSS . - Zero Inadvertent Attack Surface : Rejects arbitrary client payloads. Transmits only a fixed, deterministic verification banner PORTPROBE: TCP CONNECTION SUCCESSFUL\n and immediately reclaims connection slots. - Enterprise Security Compliance : Built-in TLS 1.3 encryption, mTLS client verification, CIDR ingress filtering, POSIX privilege dropping setuid / setgid , and constant-time Bearer token authentication. - Observability & Automation : Structured JSON logging formatted for SIEM ingestion Splunk, Elastic, Datadog , Prometheus /metrics exposition, and automated client health checking with binary exit codes. --- 4. Key Capabilities & Functional Matrix PortProbe provides a rich set of built-in capabilities tailored for enterprise operations: | Capability Domain | Implemented Features in PortProbe 2.0.0 | Operational Benefit | | :--- | :--- | :--- | | TCP Listener Management | Multi-port listening --ports 80,443,8080-8085 , single port --port , flexible IP binding --bind 127.0.0.1 or 0.0.0.0 , dual-stack I

title: System Architecture
content: Document Reference: PORTPROBE-DOC-ARC-02 Document Version: 2.0.0 Classification: Enterprise Systems Architecture Specification Status: Official Release Last Updated: November 2026 --- 1. High-Level System Architecture PortProbe is designed as an asynchronous, non-blocking network verification system built on the Tokio asynchronous runtime and the Clap command-line interface framework. Its architecture strictly decouples admission control, transport negotiation, session handling, and administrative observability. --- 2. Component Architecture & Module Responsibilities The codebase is organized into four core modules, each maintaining strict separation of concerns: Module Breakdown: | Module | Primary Structs & Types | Functional Responsibility | | :--- | :--- | :--- | | src/main.rs | main , async main args | Orchestrates single-threaded logger initialization, configuration file loading, default resolution, runtime initialization, health probe branching, privilege dropping execution, and server loop kickoff. | | src/cli.rs | Cli , ConfigFile , Cidr , LogFormat | Implements Clap derive parser; validates timeouts 1–3600s , global concurrency 1–10,000 , per-IP concurrency 1–1,000 , global rates 1–1,000 req/s , and per-IP rates 1–1,000 req/s ; parses CIDR subnets IPv4, IPv6, IPv4-mapped IPv6 ; resolves multi-port ranges 8080-8085 ; enforces POSIX file permission checks 0600 / 0400 on secrets. | | src/server.rs | ServerParams , ServerContext , TokenBucket , PerIpRateLimiter , Metrics , ConnectionStream | Manages multi-port socket2 socket configuration SO REUSEADDR hardening on Windows ; executes admission control pipeline; implements Rustls TLS 1.3 / mTLS transport; manages administrative HTTP /metrics and /healthz endpoints; processes SIGHUP configuration reload; executes client health check probes. | | src/logger.rs | init logger format , LogFormat | Safely determines local UTC timezone offset in single-threaded context; configures tracing-subscriber with EnvFilter RUST LOG ; formats records as compact terminal text or SIEM-ready JSON Lines. | --- 3. Asynchronous Execution & Concurrency Model PortProbe leverages Tokio's multi-threaded work-stealing runtime rt-multi-thread . 3.1 Socket Ingestion Architecture To handle multi-port listening across up to 50 distinct ports without thread starvation: 1. Sockets are opened via socket2::Socket , configured for non-blocking I/O, bound to the interface, and converted into asynchronous tokio::net::TcpListener instances. 2. For each listening socket, an independent, lightweight Tokio task is spawned that continuously calls listener.accept . 3. Accepted raw TcpStream, SocketAddr pairs are pushed into a bounded Tokio MPSC channel tokio::sync::mpsc::channel sized to max connections . 4. The central server event loop consumes from this MPSC channel, feeding new connections into the sequential admission control pipeline. --- 4. Admission Control Pipeline Deep Dive Every incoming TCP connection must pass through five rigorous admission gates before any worker task is allocated: Detailed Gate Mechanics: 1. Gate 1: CIDR Ingress Filter : - Compares client IP against configured subnets allow cidr . - Supports IPv4 subnets, IPv6 subnets, single host IPs, and dual-stack IPv4-mapped IPv6 ::ffff:192.168.1.1 . - Evaluation is executed under an asynchronous read lock tokio::sync::RwLock , allowing zero-downtime hot-reloads on SIGHUP. 2. Gate 2: Per-IP Token Bucket Rate Limiter : - Enforces a dedicated token bucket for each remote IP default: 5 tokens/second . - IPv6 Subnet Aggregation : To prevent attackers from evading per-IP limits by rotating IPv6 host addresses, IPv6 addresses are aggregated to their /64 routing prefix. - Throttled Hash-Map Eviction : Cleanup is executed at most once every 10 seconds, retaining only buckets refreshed within 60 seconds. A hard cap of 5,000 buckets prevents memory exhaustion. 3. Gate 3: Global Token Bucket Rate Limiter : - Enforces smooth global connection throughput default: 20 tokens/second, max 1,000 . - Computes sub-millisecond micro-tokens based on Instant::now elapsed time, preventing burst starvation. 4. Gate 4: Global Semaphore Concurrency Cap : - Uses Arc tokio::sync::Semaphore initialized with max connections default: 100, max 10,000 . - Acquired permits are owned try acquire owned and moved into the connection task, guaranteeing automatic release upon task termination. 5. Gate 5: Per-IP Concurrency Counter : - Mutex-protected HashMap IpAddr, usize . - Tracks active sessions per IP against max connections per ip default: 10 . - Wrapped in an RAII PerIpGuard struct whose Drop implementation safely decrements and removes the entry even if a task panics. --- 5. TCP Connection Lifecycle & Anti-Slowloris Architecture Once admitted, the connection lifecycle depends on whether --hold-open is enabled: 5.1 Default One-Shot Mode hold open = false In default mode, PortProbe transmits PORTPROBE: TCP CONNECTION SUCCESSFUL\n and immediately initiates socket

content: Document Reference: PORTPROBE-DOC-TCH-03 Document Version: 2.0.0 Classification: Deep-Dive Technical Implementation Manual Status: Official Release Last Updated: November 2026 --- 1. Internal State & Memory Model PortProbe is architected to guarantee thread safety, zero data races, and zero memory corruption without relying on a garbage collector or runtime lock contention. 1.1 State Ownership Hierarchy --- 2. Token Bucket Rate Limiting Algorithm PortProbe avoids the burst vulnerabilities associated with fixed-window counters which permit 2x traffic bursts across window boundaries by implementing an exact continuous-time Token Bucket Algorithm computed in micro-tokens. 2.1 Micro-Token Mathematics - Standard token buckets increment discrete integer tokens every second. Under high concurrency, integer division can cause rounding errors and token drift. - PortProbe defines: $$\text{MICRO\ TOKENS\ PER\ TOKEN} = 1,000,000$$ $$\text{max\ micro\ tokens} = \text{refill\ rate} \times 1,000,000$$ - When an incoming connection arrives at time $t {\text{now}}$, the elapsed time $\Delta t$ since $t {\text{last}}$ is computed in nanoseconds: $$\text{added\ micro\ tokens} = \frac{\Delta t {\text{nanos}} \times \text{refill\ rate}}{1000}$$ - If tokens are added: $$\text{new\ tokens} = \min \text{current\ tokens} + \text{added\ tokens}, \text{max\ tokens} $$ - A connection requires exactly $1,000,000$ micro-tokens. If available, $1,000,000$ micro-tokens are subtracted and try acquire returns true ; otherwise it returns false . 2.2 Per-IP Rate Limiting & IPv6 Prefix Aggregation To prevent an aggressive client from starving the global token bucket: 1. Every client IP is canonicalized IPv4-mapped IPv6 addresses like ::ffff:192.0.2.1 are mapped directly to 192.0.2.1 . 2. Native IPv6 addresses are masked to their /64 routing prefix via rate limit key : This prevents malicious actors from circumventing per-IP rate limiting by cycling through the $2^{64}$ host addresses in their allocated subnet. 3. Throttled Hash-Map Garbage Collection : - Running map-wide cleanups on every connection creates $O N $ CPU spikes. - PortProbe checks Instant::now .duration since last cleanup = 10s . - If 10 seconds have elapsed, it retains only buckets active within the last 60 seconds. - If the map exceeds 5,000 entries, it evicts fully refilled buckets down to 4,000 entries. --- 3. Mutual Exclusion & Poisoning Resilience A known failure mode in multi-threaded software is mutex poisoning: if a thread panics while holding a standard std::sync::Mutex , subsequent threads attempting to acquire the lock will panic on .unwrap , bringing down the entire daemon. PortProbe eliminates this risk across all synchronized structures: 3.1 Per-IP Connection Tracker PerIpTracker In PerIpGuard::drop : Even if a connection task panics, the poisoned lock is safely reclaimed via .into inner , guaranteeing that per-IP connection slots are decremented and never leaked. 3.2 Administrative Rate Limiter In start admin server : Guarantees administrative endpoints remain accessible even if an internal worker task experiences a panic. --- 4. Constant-Time Cryptographic Verification To mitigate timing side-channel attacks on the administrative endpoint, PortProbe avoids naive string comparisons == . When evaluating the HTTP Authorization: Bearer token header: 1. Both the candidate token and the expected token are hashed using SHA-256 via ring::digest::digest : 2. The fixed-length 32-byte digests are compared in constant time using subtle::ConstantTimeEq : This guarantees that token comparison execution time is strictly independent of token length or prefix matches, completely defeating timing analysis. --- 5. X.509 Certificate DER / ASN.1 Expiration Parser Rather than pulling in heavy OpenSSL or X.509 parsing dependencies, PortProbe implements a focused, zero-allocation ASN.1 parser to extract certificate expiration dates directly from the raw DER bytes: --- 6. Multi-Port Socket Range Resolver The CLI range resolver resolve all ports in src/cli.rs handles flexible input specifications: - Discrete values: 80 , 443 . - Continuous ranges: 8080-8085 . - Safety guards: - Validates ports are between 1 and 65,535. - Rejects inverted ranges e.g., 8085-8080 . - Limits any single range span to 100 ports end - start = 100 . - Deduplicates overlapping ports resolved.sort unstable ; resolved.dedup . - Hard-caps the total number of bound listening ports to 50 sockets resolved.len = 50 to protect the host against file descriptor exhaustion. --- 7. Unified Stream Abstraction ConnectionStream To handle plain TCP, TLS server connections, and TLS client health checks uniformly without dynamic dispatch dyn overhead, PortProbe encapsulates stream types in an enum implementing tokio::io::AsyncRead and tokio::io::AsyncWrite : This guarantees optimal branch prediction and inline polling in the Tokio reactor.

title: User Guide Overview
content: Document Reference: PORTPROBE-DOC-UG-01 Document Version: 2.0.0 Classification: Comprehensive User Manual Status: Official Release Last Updated: November 2026 --- 1. Guide Structure & Navigation The PortProbe User Guide is divided into dedicated modules covering every functional aspect of daemon operations, client probing, network verification, and telemetry: --- 2. Core Concepts and Terminology To make the most of PortProbe, familiarize yourself with these key terms: - Daemon Mode : The default mode of PortProbe. Binds one or more TCP listening sockets, applies admission control, responds with the PortProbe success banner, and records telemetry. - Client Probe Mode --health-check : Client execution mode. PortProbe connects to a remote or local PortProbe listener, validates the success banner, and exits with a standard return code 0 for success, 1 for failure . - Banner : The deterministic message sent by PortProbe upon establishing a valid TCP session: - Silent Rejection --silent-reject : When an unauthorized client connects e.g., from an unlisted CIDR subnet or after exhausting rate limits , PortProbe immediately drops the TCP socket without sending an error banner. This prevents automated port scanners like Nmap or Shodan from fingerprinting the host. - Immediate Reclamation --hold-open false : The default anti-Slowloris behavior where PortProbe writes its banner and initiates immediate socket shutdown, preventing clients from exhausting connection slots by keeping sockets open. - Hold-Open Mode --hold-open true : Diagnostic mode where PortProbe maintains the TCP connection until --timeout expires, allowing engineers to verify firewall state tables and idle session timeouts. - Admission Control : The 5-stage sequential validation pipeline executed on every incoming connection before allocating worker resources CIDR filter - Per-IP rate limiter - Global rate limiter - Global connection cap - Per-IP connection cap .

title: Daemon Management
content: Document Reference: PORTPROBE-DOC-UG-02 Document Version: 2.0.0 Classification: Comprehensive User Manual Status: Official Release Last Updated: November 2026 --- 1. Starting the Daemon The PortProbe daemon is started simply by invoking portprobe with the desired port or configuration options. 1.1 Single Port Listening To listen on a single port e.g., port 8080 : By default, PortProbe binds exclusively to 127.0.0.1 localhost to ensure security. 1.2 Listening on All Network Interfaces To accept incoming connections across all physical and virtual interfaces e.g., for remote firewall testing : !WARNING When --bind 0.0.0.0 or --bind :: is used, PortProbe logs a prominent warning: Listening on all interfaces. Ensure firewall restrictions are configured. Always combine wildcard bindings with --allow-cidr or external firewall rules. --- 2. Multi-Port and Port Range Listening PortProbe supports binding multiple discrete ports and continuous port ranges simultaneously in a single daemon process. Syntax: --ports PORTS The --ports argument accepts a comma-separated list of individual port numbers and port ranges: Safety Rules & Validation: 1. Range Bounds : Port numbers must be between 1 and 65535 . 2. Range Direction : The start port must be less than or equal to the end port 8080-8085 is valid; 8085-8080 is rejected . 3. Range Span Cap : A single range cannot exceed 100 ports end - start = 100 . 4. Global Port Limit : The total number of unique listening sockets cannot exceed 50 ports . 5. Deduplication : If overlapping ports are specified e.g., --port 8080 --ports "8080-8082" , PortProbe automatically sorts and deduplicates the list to 8080, 8081, 8082 . Startup Log Output: --- 3. Dynamic Configuration Reload SIGHUP On Linux/Unix systems, PortProbe supports live configuration reloading without dropping the running process or disconnecting active TCP sessions. Triggering SIGHUP: Dynamically Reloadable Parameters: 1. CIDR Subnet Rules allow cidr : When updated in portprobe.toml , SIGHUP parses and hot-reloads the new allowlist into the active RwLock . New connections immediately adhere to the updated subnet rules. 2. TLS Server Certificate & Key tls cert , tls key : When certificates are renewed e.g., via Let's Encrypt or corporate PKI , SIGHUP reloads the certificates, rebuilds the TlsAcceptor , and updates the certificate expiration gauge without dropping the listener. Reload Log Output: --- 4. Privilege Dropping POSIX / Linux Running network tools as root is a major violation of security compliance standards CIS Benchmarks, NIST SP 800-53 . However, binding privileged ports ports 1024 like 80 or 443 requires root privileges at startup. PortProbe solves this using post-socket-bind privilege dropping: How It Works: 1. PortProbe starts with root privileges EUID 0 and binds ports 80 and 443. 2. Before accepting any client connections, PortProbe executes drop privileges , which permanently transitions the process UID and GID to the unprivileged portprobe account. 3. If running as root and privilege dropping fails, the daemon strictly aborts to prevent executing unprivileged workloads with elevated privileges. 4. If already running as an unprivileged user, the privilege drop is safely skipped with an informational log. --- 5. Graceful Daemon Shutdown To stop PortProbe safely without terminating in-flight connections: - Send SIGINT Ctrl+C or SIGTERM . Shutdown Sequence: 1. Listening sockets stop accepting new incoming connections. 2. The internal shutdown watch channel broadcasts true to all active worker tasks. 3. Active worker tasks complete their current response transmission. 4. The metrics summary table is emitted to the logger. 5. PortProbe exits with ExitCode::SUCCESS 0 .

Detailed Diagnostic Scenarios & Resolutions Scenario 1: Daemon Fails to Start - "Address already in use" - Symptoms : PortProbe exits with code 1; log shows: Failed to accept connection on 0.0.0.0:8080: Address already in use os error 98 - Possible Causes : Another application e.g., Nginx, Tomcat, another PortProbe instance is already bound to that port. - Diagnostic Steps : - Resolution : Stop the competing process, or configure PortProbe to listen on an alternative port e.g., --port 8081 . --- Scenario 2: Client Receives "Connection Refused" - Symptoms : Client running nc -vz server-ip 8080 or portprobe --health-check reports: Connection refused os error 111 - Possible Causes : 1. PortProbe is bound to 127.0.0.1 localhost only instead of 0.0.0.0 or the network interface IP. 2. PortProbe daemon is not running. - Diagnostic Steps : - Resolution : Restart PortProbe with --bind 0.0.0.0 or the specific host IP. --- Scenario 3: Client Receives "Connection Timeout" - Symptoms : Client hangs for 30–60 seconds, then reports connection timeout. - Possible Causes : 1. A network firewall iptables, firewalld, AWS Security Group, Palo Alto firewall is silently dropping packets DROP action . 2. Routing table is missing a return route back to the client subnet. - Diagnostic Steps : - Resolution : Update intermediate firewall access rules or routing table entries. --- Scenario 4: Unauthorized Connections Dropped Silently - Symptoms : Client connects, but the connection closes immediately without receiving any banner or data. - Possible Causes : 1. PortProbe has --silent-reject true enabled default , and the client IP is not included in --allow-cidr . 2. The client exceeded --max-rate-per-ip or --max-connections-per-ip . - Diagnostic Steps : Check daemon logs with debug verbosity RUST LOG=debug portprobe ... : - Resolution : Add the client IP or subnet to allow cidr , or adjust rate limits. --- Scenario 5: Insecure File Permissions Error - Symptoms : Startup fails with: Configuration error: Insecure permissions on /etc/portprobe/admin token.secret: 644. headings: How does PortProbe differ from Netcat (nc -l)?

content: Document Reference: PORTPROBE-DOC-TRB-02 Document Version: 2.0.0 Classification: Operational Troubleshooting Manual Status: Official Release Last Updated: November 2026 --- 1. General Questions What is PortProbe? PortProbe is an asynchronous TCP connectivity verification utility written in Rust. It allows infrastructure teams to test network reachability, verify firewall rules, and validate load balancers without deploying full enterprise workloads. How does PortProbe differ from Netcat nc -l ? Netcat lacks concurrency caps, rate limiting, CIDR ingress filtering, structured JSON logging, TLS 1.3/mTLS support, multi-port binding, and administrative telemetry endpoints. Netcat can also be exploited to receive arbitrary payloads or crash servers. PortProbe provides a hardened, enterprise-grade architecture. Does PortProbe support UDP? PortProbe 2.0.0 supports TCP and TLS-over-TCP only. UDP connectivity verification is planned for a future release see Release Notes . --- 2. Security Questions Can PortProbe be exploited to execute remote commands? No. PortProbe strictly rejects client payloads. In default mode, it transmits its static banner PORTPROBE: TCP CONNECTION SUCCESSFUL\n and immediately shuts down the socket. It never parses or executes client input. Why does PortProbe drop connections without sending an error banner? By default, --silent-reject is set to true . This prevents automated scanners like Nmap or Shodan from fingerprinting PortProbe or identifying which ports are actively listening. If you need explicit error banners for debugging, set --silent-reject false . How does PortProbe authenticate administrative requests? PortProbe uses constant-time cryptographic Bearer token authentication subtle::ConstantTimeEq combined with SHA-256 pre-hashing , completely mitigating timing attacks. --- 3. Operations & Configuration How can I reload firewall CIDR rules without restarting PortProbe? On Linux/Unix systems, edit /etc/portprobe/portprobe.toml and send SIGHUP to the process: PortProbe will reload the CIDR allowlist and TLS certificates in-flight without dropping active connections. Why do I get "Too many open files" errors? Each concurrent connection requires an OS file descriptor. Raise your system limits: Or in systemd : Can I run PortProbe as a Windows Service? Yes. Although native Windows Service Control Manager dispatching --service is pending in version 2.1.0, you can run PortProbe as a reliable Windows Service today using NSSM Non-Sucking Service Manager . See docs/getting-started/installation.md ../getting-started/installation.md .

title: Developer Architecture
content: Document Reference: PORTPROBE-DOC-DEV-01 Document Version: 2.0.0 Classification: Developer Manual Status: Official Release Last Updated: November 2026 --- 1. Codebase Organization The PortProbe repository follows standard Rust idiomatic structure: --- 2. Core Dependencies & Technology Stack | Dependency | Version | Purpose in PortProbe | | :--- | :--- | :--- | | tokio | 1.x | Asynchronous runtime rt-multi-thread , net , time , signal , sync . | | clap | 4.x | Command-line argument parsing with derive macros and environment variable support. | | tracing / tracing-subscriber | 0.1 / 0.3 | Structured diagnostic event logging with JSON Lines formatting and env filtering. | | tokio-rustls / rustls-pki-types | 0.26 / 1.x | Pure-Rust TLS 1.3 / 1.2 asynchronous encryption engine without OpenSSL C-bindings. | | socket2 | 0.6 | Low-level OS socket creation, dual-stack IPv6, and SO REUSEADDR configuration. | | subtle | 2.6 | Constant-time cryptographic comparison primitives ConstantTimeEq . | | ring | 0.17 | Cryptographic SHA-256 digest computation for constant-time token hashing. | | serde / toml | 1.x / 0.8 | Deserialization of declarative TOML configuration files. | | time | 0.3 | Thread-safe RFC 3339 local timezone timestamp formatting. | | privdrop / nix | 0.5 / 0.30 | Safe POSIX privilege dropping and EUID inspection on Unix systems. | --- 3. Coding Conventions & Invariants All contributions must strictly adhere to the following architectural invariants: 1. Zero Unsafe Code : ! deny unsafe code is enforced at the crate root in src/main.rs . PRs containing unsafe blocks will be rejected by automated CI compiler gates. 2. Deterministic Cryptography : Never use variable-time string comparisons == when evaluating authentication tokens. Always hash candidate strings with SHA-256 and evaluate with subtle::ConstantTimeEq . 3. Mutex Poisoning Resilience : Never call .unwrap directly on a standard Mutex lock in long-lived server code. Always handle poisoned locks gracefully via .unwrap or else |p| p.into inner . 4. Error Handling : Use Result T, String or Result T, Box dyn std::error::Error + Send + Sync . Return std::process::ExitCode::SUCCESS or ExitCode::FAILURE from main . 5. Logging Levels : - error! : Unrecoverable errors that terminate the daemon or invalidate configuration. - warn! : Significant security events TLS handshake failure, privileged port warnings, deprecated CLI token usage . - info! : Connection lifecycle events started, accepted, success response sent, shutdown . - debug! : Granular diagnostics CIDR drops, rate limit drops, EOF detections, byte counts .

Version 2.0.0 Release Summary PortProbe 2.0.0 represents a major enterprise release, transitioning the utility from a basic single-port listener into a hardened, high-concurrency, asynchronous connectivity daemon and client probe built on Rust 2021 and Tokio. Key Highlights of Version 2.0.0: - Multi-Port & Port Range Listening --ports : Simultaneous binding across discrete ports and ranges up to 50 listening sockets. - Pure-Rust TLS 1.3 & mTLS --tls-cert , --tls-key , --tls-client-ca : Integrated asynchronous TLS engine with client certificate verification and automated certificate expiration tracking. - Client Probe Mode --health-check : Native client testing mode with TLS SNI verification and standard OS exit codes. - Administrative HTTP Server --admin-port : Embedded Prometheus /metrics and /healthz endpoints with constant-time Bearer token authentication. - Advanced Admission Control : Token-bucket rate limiting global and per-IP , semaphore concurrency caps, and IPv6 /64 prefix aggregation. - Zero-Fingerprint Reconnaissance Protection --silent-reject : Drops unauthorized connections immediately at the TCP socket layer without transmitting diagnostic error banners. - Anti-Slowloris Architecture --hold-open false : Immediate connection slot reclamation post-banner transmission by default. - Dynamic Configuration Hot-Reload SIGHUP : Live updating of CIDR allowlists and TLS certificates without dropping the daemon. - POSIX Privilege Dropping --user , --group : Securely drops root privileges post-socket-bind. --- 2. title: Known Limitations
content: Document Reference: PORTPROBE-DOC-REL-02 Document Version: 2.0.0 Classification: Release Specification Status: Official Release Last Updated: November 2026 --- 1. Verified Implementation Gaps & Limitations To ensure engineering transparency and operational safety, the following known limitations in PortProbe 2.0.0 are documented along with their operational mitigations: 1.1 Windows Service Flag --service - Limitation : The --service flag is declared in src/cli.rs:253 , but src/main.rs does not currently invoke the Windows Service Control Manager SCM dispatcher. Running portprobe --service in Windows PowerShell starts in standard console mode. - Operational Workaround : To deploy PortProbe as a resilient background service on Windows Server, install it using NSSM Non-Sucking Service Manager or Windows Task Scheduler at system boot. See docs/getting-started/installation.md ../getting-started/installation.md . 1.2 Administrative Server TLS - Limitation : The administrative HTTP endpoint --admin-port operates over plain HTTP on 127.0.0.1 . It does not support TLS encryption directly. - Operational Workaround : PortProbe strictly binds the administrative server to 127.0.0.1 localhost , ensuring traffic does not leave the local loopback interface. If remote Prometheus scraping is required, route requests through a reverse proxy e.g., Nginx, Envoy or SSH tunnel. 1.3 Transport Protocol Scope No UDP Support - Limitation : PortProbe 2.0.0 exclusively verifies TCP and TLS-over-TCP reachability. It does not support UDP port reachability testing e.g., DNS port 53, SNMP port 161 . - Operational Workaround : For UDP reachability verification, continue using traditional tools such as nc -u or specialized UDP probes until UDP support is released in PortProbe 2.2.0. 1.4 Windows File Permission Validation - Limitation : The secret file permission check verify file permissions in src/cli.rs validates POSIX octal file modes 0600 / 0400 . On Windows, this check is a no-op because Windows uses NTFS Discretionary Access Control Lists DACLs . - Operational Workaround : Administrators on Windows Server must ensure that secret token files and TLS private keys have restricted NTFS permissions via icacls , granting read access exclusively to the service account or SYSTEM . 1.5 Dynamic SIGHUP Reload on Windows - Limitation : Operating system signals like SIGHUP are POSIX-specific and not supported by Windows kernels. - Operational Workaround : On Windows Server, configuration updates require a service restart via Restart-Service PortProbe or NSSM.
